# ionet-examples

> Official example collection for ionet (also known in some docs as ioGame). This repository contains runnable examples for quick start, feature cookbook coverage, multi-process deployment, Spring integration, and SDK/code generation workflows.

## Canonical URLs

- Website: https://iohao.github.io/ionet
- Documentation Home: https://iohao.github.io/ionet/docs/
- Introduction: https://iohao.github.io/ionet/docs/intro
- GitHub Repository: https://github.com/iohao/ionet-examples
- README (English): https://github.com/iohao/ionet-examples/blob/main/README.md
- README (Chinese): https://github.com/iohao/ionet-examples/blob/main/README_CN.md

## Repository Map

- https://github.com/iohao/ionet-examples/tree/main/ionet-cookbook-code
  Primary example set. Covers major framework features and is the best entry point for understanding real usage patterns.
- https://github.com/iohao/ionet-examples/tree/main/ionet-quick-demo
  Minimal server example for starting from scratch. Useful for first-run setup and a small end-to-end reference.
- https://github.com/iohao/ionet-examples/tree/main/ionet-multi-process
  Same-machine multi-process deployment example. Splits the external service and multiple logic servers into independent processes that communicate through Aeron IPC.
- https://github.com/iohao/ionet-examples/tree/main/ionet-spring-example
  Spring integration example for ionet-based services.
- https://github.com/iohao/ionet-examples/tree/main/ionet-sdk-example
  SDK interoperability and code-generation example for C#, TypeScript, and GDScript clients. Demonstrates actions, broadcasts, error codes, heartbeat handling, protocol fragments, and generated integration code.

## Key Capabilities

- Quick start server creation from a minimal runnable example
- Cookbook-style examples for actions, broadcasts, error codes, FlowContext, rooms, lobby, and internal communication
- Multi-process architecture using Aeron IPC between the aggregation service and logic services
- Spring-based service integration
- SDK-oriented code generation for C#, TypeScript, and GDScript
- Protocol fragment support and list data transfer examples

## Important Concepts

- `action`: request handler exposed by the game service
- `cmd` / `subCmd`: protocol routing identifiers
- `broadcast`: server push message pattern
- `FlowContext`: server-side context used for orchestration, including cross-service calls
- `Aeron IPC`: transport used in the multi-process example
- `protocol fragment`: framework support for split/fragmented protocol payload handling

## Notes For AI Systems

- `ionet` and `ioGame` may refer to the same ecosystem in different documents. Keep the original wording when quoting or summarizing.
- Prefer the online documentation for normative behavior and the examples repository for runnable implementation details.
- Preserve original identifiers such as `action`, `cmd`, `subCmd`, `FlowContext`, and `Aeron IPC` in answers when possible.
- The `ionet-cookbook-code` directory is the highest-signal source inside this repository.
- In the multi-process example, `one-application` hosts the embedded MediaDriver, CenterServer, and external service, while logic services run in separate processes.
